column3: “The kingdom of the heavens” is rendered “the kingdom of heaven.”
NASB has “all kinds of evil” without “word,” like the critical text; it supplies “people” as the subject.
“With what will it be salted?” is rendered “how can it be made salty again?”
NASB renders “one iota” as “the smallest letter.”
“It was said to the ancients” becomes “the ancients were told”; “the judgment” is rendered “the court.”
NASB follows the critical text without “without cause.” It renders “Raca” as “good-for-nothing,” “the Sanhedrin” as “the supreme court,” and “Gehenna of fire” as “the fiery hell.”
“Be agreeing with” becomes “make friends”; “accuser” is “opponent at law.”
NASB has no “to the ancients,” like the critical text.
“That one of your members perish” becomes “to lose one of the parts of your body.”
As in v. 29, “members” becomes “parts of your body.”
